## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. What the ayah states  (`#what-the-ayah-states`)

Cited ayat: 2:102

> **2:102** وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَا تَتْلُوا۟ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَٰرُوتَ وَمَٰرُوتَ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَآ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِۦ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِۦ وَمَا هُم بِضَآرِّينَ بِهِۦ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا۟ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا۟ بِهِۦٓ أَنفُسَهُمْ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:102): Some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman.

**c2** (2:102): Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery.

**c3** (2:102): They also followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut.

**c4** (2:102): They did not teach anyone until they had said that they were only a trial, and that he should therefore not disbelieve.

**c5** (2:102): People learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they harm no one by it except by God's permission.

**c6** (2:102): They learned what harms them and does not benefit them, and they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew.

### One-minute summary

The ayah says that some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman, and that Sulayman did not disbelieve [c1][c2]. It also says that they followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut, who taught no one until they had said that they were only a trial [c3][c4].

### Complete story

Some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman [c1]. Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery [c2]. They also followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut [c3]. They did not teach anyone until they had said that they were only a trial, and that he should therefore not disbelieve [c4]. People learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they harm no one by it except by God's permission [c5]. They learned what harms them and does not benefit them, and they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew [c6].

### Deep study

The ayah is one long sentence, and it does not say who the people are who followed what the devils recited [c1]. The Arabic word for the pair can be read as angels or as kings in different recitations [c3]. The Arabic word ma can be read as what or as not, and the sense of the clause changes with it [c3].

### Kids mode

Sulayman did not disbelieve [c2]. The ayah says that Harut and Marut told anyone who came to them that they were only a trial, so that he should not disbelieve [c4]. It says that whoever buys what harms him has no share in the Hereafter [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah separates Sulayman from disbelief and puts the teaching of sorcery on the devils [c2]. Another is that it presents what people learned as harming them and not benefiting them [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the people are who followed what the devils recited, or when this happened.
- Not established: whether the Arabic is to be read as angels or kings, or whether what was sent down is affirmed or denied; the recitations and the readers differ, and this draft does not choose.
- Not established: where Babil was, or what the trial consisted of.
- Not established: anything about their nature, what they taught beyond the words of the ayah, or what became of them.
